answer.rationale: The incumbent's refusal to reopen pricing combined with the 18% spend mandate makes renegotiation unlikely to succeed (memory_c4 worked previously, but leverage has diminished). memory_c2 demonstrates that the low-cost vendor successfully delivered sharp unit cost reduction with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing. With 14 days remaining, switching to the proven low-cost vendor is the only path to meet the 18% cost target. The 94% volume utilization creates delivery risk, but memory_c2's track record through the shortage and memory_c5's successful month-to-month deferral suggest operational resilience is possible. A standard_experiment scale allows monitoring the transition closely over the next 30–60 days before full commitment, protecting against hidden onboarding friction while capturing the cost savings the mandate requires. Deferring (memory_c5) is not viable given the hard deadline and budget pressure. Adding a second source (memory_c3) addresses resilience but not cost. Renewing (memory_c1) violates the cost mandate.
